messages:
michael_csm: Quick sync — Pinegrove QBR is next Wed 11AM PT. I want a short pre-QBR triage today: token econ for their embeddings-heavy pipeline, 90-day spend forecast, onboarding gaps (theyre still on the pilot SDK), renewal risk indicators, and a feedback capture plan. Can we do 30m at 2:30pm PT? cc @rachel_fin @li_eng @yana_enable

rachel_fin: 2:30 works. Billing alert: invoicing flag popped yesterday (B-10222). Current run rate ~ $7.6k/mo, embeddings ~ 73% of spend. If they flip batch to real-time, estimate ~ x1.7 (~$13k/mo). I'll prepare a commit vs on-demand note.

li_eng: I can join. From engineering notes: Pinegrove is using SDK v0.9 (pilot) which doesn't include prefix caching and has a bug where retries re-run embeddings. That explains part of the spike. I'll prep a tiny patch and a demo snippet.

yana_enable: Onboarding status: they completed basic auth but haven't wired server-side debounce or memoization. Also they asked for a short enablement workshop—we should include that in the QBR ask list. I'll draft a short checklist.

pm_pinegrove: FYI — PM here. We're worried about a surprise invoice before renewal. We want options to control cost without hurting latency for users. Happy to join the triage.

michael_csm: Great, invite sent. Agenda for 30m: 1) run-rate + two scenarios (x1.3, x1.7) 2) immediate levers (KV caching, debounce/aggregation, per-route soft quotas, small commit options) 3) enablement plan + who will run the workshop 4) capture PM feedback & sign-offs.

rachel_fin: Quick forecast (rough):
- current: $7.6k/mo
- x1.3 -> $9.9k/mo
- x1.7 -> $12.9k/mo
Assumes avg 2 vectors/request @512-d. I'll attach the CSV breakdown in the triage thread.

li_eng: Minimal caching snippet (py) to show in demo:
```
# very small prefix KV cache
if prefix in kv:
  return kv[prefix]
vec = embeddings.embed(prefix)
kv[prefix] = vec
return vec
```
Also proposing adding Idempotency-Key header to stop duplicate retries.

yana_enable: Enablement checklist preview: 1) Add KV cache + sample code 2) Debounce/aggregate webhooks to batch embeddings 3) Short workshop (45m) for infra + app team 4) Post-QBR follow-up: 2-week enablement sprint. I'll own workshop scheduling.

billing-bot: Alert: Pinegrove usage increased 78% yesterday vs baseline 0 triggered rule embed_spike_high. See https://redwood.ops/alerts/10222

michael_csm: Rachel please post commit vs on-demand table and a proposed small burst reserve number before the meeting. Li please paste a tiny SDK patch gist link. Yana, can you set proposed workshop times? PM, would you prefer a workshop before or after QBR?

pm_pinegrove: Prefer before the QBR if possible. We can do a 45m slot tomorrow afternoon PST. That should help narrow mitigations to present to our execs.

rachel_fin: Draft commit options (preview): 1) 3mo small commit - ~7% cost reduction vs on-demand at current run-rate 2) 6mo mid commit - ~12% reduction but requires tighter forecasting 3) Burst reserve for nightly jobs - $1k/mo reserve reduces on-demand exposure for scheduled batches. Will publish numbers in doc /shared/finance/pinegrove-commit-options.

li_eng: Patch gist: https://redwood.internal/gists/pinegrove-prefix-cache-patch - adds simple cache + idempotency header. Low-risk, can be hotfixed into their app or we can push to SDK v1.0 in the enablement sprint.

yana_enable: I'll propose two workshop slots: Tomorrow 1:30PM PT or 4:00PM PT. I'll ping PM directly and confirm. Also will draft a short feedback form to capture their priorities and acceptance criteria for mitigations.

michael_csm: Nice. Action owners: Rachel -> commit math + pre-read; Li -> demo patch + per-route CSV; Yana -> workshop scheduling + feedback form; Michael -> send pre-read + invite to customer execs. PM to confirm workshop time.

pm_pinegrove: Confirm 4:00PM PT tomorrow works for our engineering lead. Please include the forecast table and suggested quick-wins in the invite.

michael_csm: Done. I'll attach Rachel's table and Li's gist. Locking 2:30pm triage now and workshop tomorrow 4:00PM PT. If someone can't make, post notes here. End.
